properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): when a newer reflow2 opens a design, it KNOWS the version that served it before (the store's stamp, and the old daemon's rendezvous on a re-election) and says so only to stderr, then overwrites the stamp. served_by carries only the opposite case (behind_record, lifted 2026-09-15). So an upgrade under a live conversation reads as normal, and the evidence is gone after one open
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-09-28, triaging art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28 (hxm_program hub, addendum dated 2026-09-11, reflow2 0.56.0 → 0.58.0) under rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words: "after a `/mcp` reconnect the served version was **0.58.0** and two tools appeared that were not in the 0.56.0 surface (`relation_coverage`, `repair_report`) ... That the version can move under a running session without the session noticing, unless it re-reads the stamp, is itself mild feedback: `served_by` reports `stale` for a replaced *binary*, but a reconnect to a newer daemon reads as normal." EXPECTED: the first read after the move says the design is now served by a different reflow2 than before, so skills and tool descriptions read earlier may be out of date. NOT AFFECTED: served_by.reflow2_version was correct (0.58.0), and stale=false was true of the new process.

② PRECEDENT (searched on the reporter's words): cap:the-server-knows-its-own-currency (stale: the binary replaced under a RUNNING process); chg:a-client-replaces-a-mismatched-server-instead-of-reporting-it (2026-08-29: a client meeting a daemon of another build replaces it, so a reconnect after an upgrade lands on a fresh, current server by design); fact:the-attach-path-checks-liveness-and-identity-but-never-version; chg:an-import-knows-its-own-age-and-a-server-behind-its-record-says-so (2026-09-15: a binary BEHIND its record is surfaced as served_by.behind_record). Nothing records the AHEAD case reaching a session.

③ CANDIDATES, from the bones:
(A) GOVERNANCE/CONTRACT. The upgrade direction was judged harmless ("Additive only — everything in it still reads") because it is harmless to the DATA, so only the dangerous direction was lifted into served_by. What the SESSION needs (its tool list and skills changed) was never the question asked.
(B) SUBSTRATE. Across a reconnect the server has no memory of what served the design before, so nothing could say it moved.
(C) OUTSIDE REFLOW2. The harness re-lists tools on reconnect and does not tell the model.
(D) CHANGE. The re-election path (chg:a-client-replaces...) knows the old daemon's version and drops it.
(E) THE OBSERVATION IS WRONG. Some served read did say it and the session missed it.

④ WHAT WOULD SEPARATE THEM: (B) predicts no record of the prior version exists at open. (A) and (D) predict one exists and reaches no served read. (E) predicts a served read names the prior version.

⑤ RESULTS (0.74.0 binary, scratch store; source at 70e547f):
· Simulated the upgrade by setting the scratch store's <graph>.meta.json reflow2_version to 0.56.0, then opening it with 0.74.0. stderr, twice: "this graph was written by reflow2 0.56.0 (28 node types, 65 edge types); you are running 0.74.0 (28, 65). Additive only — everything in it still reads." loop_status.served_by: {reflow2_version 0.74.0, stale false}. Neither loop_status nor get_instructions contains "0.56.0" anywhere. After that single open, meta.json read 0.74.0: the evidence is overwritten.
· Code: Provenance::OlderGraph {was, now} is computed at every open (crates/reflow2-core/src/provenance.rs). service.rs new_reporting keeps only `provenance.newer_writer()` (the NewerWriter case) as written_by, and its own comment says why the other cases fail: "the note above is printed once to a log nobody reads mid-session, and `served_by` is what a session actually consults". OlderGraph and Unstamped go only to that log.
· Re-election (shared.rs ~456): should_reelect's reason names the old daemon's version ("versions: {} there"). It goes to tracing::warn in the client proxy's stderr, and the new daemon starts with no knowledge of it.
· The usage ledger (<graph>.usage.jsonl) records no server version per call. <graph>.client.json holds only the current version and is overwritten on every handshake.
⇒ (B) REFUTED: the prior version is known at open (the stamp) and at re-election (the rendezvous). (E) REFUTED: no served read carries it. (A) and (D) HOLD, as one cause at two sites. (C) is real but not reflow2's to fix, and fixing (A) makes it moot for reflow2's own surface.

⑥ CLASS: facts computed once at startup leave through a log, and a session reads only served replies. Of the three open-time provenance notes (Unstamped, OlderGraph, NewerWriter), one reaches served_by. The re-election reason reaches none. The 2026-09-15 fix named this class in its own comment and closed it for one variant, the one that corrupts writes. A fix at the class (every open-time note and re-election reason is kept on the service and served, e.g. served_by.moved_from {version, since} on the session's first orientation read) would have answered this report as well as the 853-edge report of 2026-09-14.

⑦ OUT OF SCOPE (no code changed). A test pinning the class would open a store whose stamp names an older version, and assert two things. First, loop_status.served_by (or get_instructions) names the prior version and says tool descriptions and skills read before may be out of date. Second, the same holds when a shared client re-elects a daemon of another build. Today both fail: 0 of 2 sites surface it.

REPORTER'S CONCLUSIONS: HELD. "stale covers a replaced binary, a reconnect to a newer daemon reads as normal" is exactly the code. SHARPENED: the server is not blind. It computes the move at open and prints it where no session looks. PROPOSED FIX (the reporter's, made concrete): keep the OlderGraph (and re-election) note on the service and serve it in served_by and loop_status.next until the session has seen it once, naming the tools added or removed where the stamps allow.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: the reporter's actual 0.56.0 → 0.58.0 transition was not reproduced. It was simulated by editing a scratch stamp, since no 0.56.0 binary is on this machine. Also not established: whether the reporter's server was shared (re-election) or stdio-direct (open-time stamp only); both paths are covered above. Whether any harness surfaces an MCP reconnect to its model was not checked.
